subject: Science

book.title: Curiosity
book.officialStructureEvidence: NCERT textbook portal lists Curiosity for Class VI Science with 12 chapter files; current 2026-27 index corroborates titles/order.
book.sourcePolicy: Chapter titles/order are curriculum mapping metadata. KirthiVerse teaching text, examples, questions, hints and remediation are independently authored; no textbook prose, figures or exercise questions are reproduced.

chapters.title: Mindful Eating: A Path to a Healthy Body
A Journey through States of Water
Methods of Separation in Everyday Life

chapter1Topics.title: Curiosity, observation and scientific questions
competencies: turn an observation into a useful question
identify questions that can be investigated with evidence
misconceptions: treating an opinion as an observation
assuming every why-question can be answered by one simple experiment

chapter1Topics.title: Testable explanations and fair investigations
competencies: identify what to change and what to observe
recognise that a prediction can be wrong without the investigation being useless
misconceptions: changing several factors at once
treating a hypothesis as a proven fact

chapter1Topics.title: Recording evidence, analysing results and revising ideas
competencies: draw a conclusion limited to the evidence
revise an explanation when evidence disagrees
misconceptions: changing results to match a prediction
calling an unexpected result a failed experiment

chapter1CompletionRule: CHAPTER1_KIKI_TEACHING_SLICE_COMPLETE requires all three mapped inquiry topics to include independently authored teaching, a worked investigation, misconception handling, linked practice/assessment, remediation/mastery evidence, deterministic QA, offline coverage and release regression coverage.

chapter2Topics.title: Observing diversity and describing variation
competencies: compare living things using multiple observable characteristics
limit generalisations to the observed sample
misconceptions: a few examples represent every member of a group
one obvious characteristic fully describes diversity

chapter2Topics.title: Classification and simple branching keys
competencies: follow and construct simple branching keys
recognise that different useful criteria can produce different groupings
misconceptions: classification can use unstated preference
there is only one perfect grouping for every purpose

chapter2Topics.title: Organisms, habitats and evidence-aware adaptation reasoning
competencies: separate observed trait from inferred function
relate habitat evidence to cautious functional hypotheses
use privacy- and conservation-aware observation practices
misconceptions: trait function is directly observed
trait plus habitat proves exact cause or evolutionary history

chapter2CompletionRule: CHAPTER2_KIKI_TEACHING_SLICE_COMPLETE requires all three mapped diversity topics to include independently authored teaching, evidence-aware examples, misconception handling, linked practice/assessment, remediation/mastery evidence, deterministic QA, offline coverage and release regression coverage.

chapter3Topics.title: Food diversity and what nutrients do
competencies: recognise food diversity across cultural meals
avoid diagnosing nutrient status from one meal
misconceptions: one food must contain every nutrient
one nutrient makes a food or person morally good/bad
one meal diagnoses a deficiency

chapter3Topics.title: Building balanced meals and mindful routines
misconceptions: balanced means identical plates
balance means restriction or skipping meals
all children should follow one calorie target

chapter3Topics.title: Food information, hygiene and evidence-aware choices
competencies: separate label facts from marketing claims
misconceptions: marketing phrases prove health outcomes
children should self-test allergens
supplements can be self-prescribed as treatment
safetyBoundary: medical dietary needs escalate to trusted adult and qualified healthcare guidance

chapter3CompletionRule: CHAPTER3_KIKI_TEACHING_SLICE_COMPLETE requires three age-appropriate nutrition-literacy topics with food diversity, balanced meal/hydration reasoning, evidence-aware food information and hygiene, misconception handling, assessment, remediation/mastery evidence, explicit child-safety exclusions for dieting/weight/calorie/diagnosis/supplements/allergy self-testing, deterministic QA, offline coverage and release regression coverage.

chapter4Topics.title: Magnetic materials and evidence
misconceptions: all metals are magnetic
shiny objects are magnetic
the outer material always explains attraction

chapter4Topics.title: Magnet poles, attraction and repulsion
competencies: use repulsion as stronger evidence of two magnets than attraction alone
misconceptions: magnets always attract
every attracted object is a magnet
one observation proves a general rule
safetyBoundary: avoid finger pinch from snapping magnets

chapter4Topics.title: Compass direction, interference and safe investigation
competencies: describe roughly north-south settling of a freely rotating magnet
interpret compass deflection from nearby magnetic influence
misconceptions: a compass reading cannot be disturbed
nearby magnet movement means geographic north moved
electronics should be dismantled to find magnets
safetyBoundary: never ingest or place magnets in mouth/nose/ears
keep small high-powered magnets away from children
follow manufacturer or qualified medical guidance around implanted medical devices

chapter4CompletionRule: CHAPTER4_KIKI_TEACHING_SLICE_COMPLETE requires three evidence-led magnet topics covering magnetic-material testing, pole attraction/repulsion and compass/direction reasoning, with misconception handling, linked assessment, remediation/mastery evidence, explicit no-ingestion/no-dismantling/high-powered-magnet safety, deterministic QA, offline coverage and release regression coverage.

chapter5Topics.title: Standard units and reliable length measurement
competencies: choose suitable metric units and instruments
calculate final minus initial for non-zero starts
misconceptions: the final ruler mark is always the object length
units can be omitted
more decimal places always mean better measurement
safetyBoundary: no measurement near traffic or moving machinery

chapter5Topics.title: Curved paths, flexible measures and estimation
competencies: choose a flexible method for curved lengths
misconceptions: a straight chord equals every curved path
repetition creates unlimited precision
an estimate is an exact measurement

chapter5Topics.title: Motion, reference points and patterns
competencies: state a reference point before deciding motion
recognise multiple motion descriptions can coexist
separate motion type from speed or cause
misconceptions: motion is absolute and reference-independent
circular and periodic mean the same thing
motion type alone determines speed

chapter5CompletionRule: CHAPTER5_KIKI_TEACHING_SLICE_COMPLETE requires three evidence-led topics covering standard-unit/ruler measurement, curved-length method/uncertainty and reference-aware motion patterns, with misconception handling, linked assessment, remediation/mastery evidence, explicit safe tabletop/classroom measurement and motion boundaries, deterministic QA, offline coverage and release regression coverage.
completionRule: SCIENCE_COMPLETE only after all twelve Curiosity chapters have Kiki-teachable coverage, age-appropriate investigations or evidence activities where applicable, practice, assessment, remediation/mastery evidence, accessibility QA and source/provenance review.
